title: Slot synchronization glitch causing intermittent batch deserts
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Summary: Between 2026-03-07 02:10 UTC and 2026-03-07 08:30 UTC a subset of production serving shards experienced recurring multi-minute periods where the continuous batching pipeline stopped emitting batches for small-low-priority traffic. We observed long tail latency spikes (P95->P99.9), fairness skew (small requests starved by large-request cohorts), and elevated error budgets for a handful of customers. This ticket tracks the incident analysis, mitigations applied, and concrete follow-ups to prevent recurrence.

Notes: timeline includes debug traces and flamegraphs linked in 'links' field.
detection: Primary signal: P99 latency spikes on responsive routes + an increase in 'batch_wait_time' histogram on specific scheduler shards. Secondary signal: metric 'slot_inflight_count' dropping to zero on affected replicas while request queues remained non-empty. Alert threshold was the latency SLO (P99>350ms) which fired for 3 customers concurrently.
root_cause: Race between the slot allocation timer and the coalescer's precedence logic during a codepath change deployed 2026-03-05. The new precedence optimization attempted to drain long-running high-token requests first; under particular timing the scheduler's slot watermark update was lost on one replica leading to persistent 'no-slot' state for low-priority queues. Contributing factors: (1) cross-shard watermark propagation relied on eventual GC windows (2) a regression in the slot-state reconciliation backoff, and (3) insufficient per-request jitter that allowed timer alignment and priority inversion across many clients.
impact: Customer-facing: P99 latency regressions for small/interactive requests on ~7% of requests routed to affected shards. Internal: increased backpressure on worker GPUs causing transient token generation delays. Operational: multiple SEs engaged for customer escalations; SLA credits evaluated for 4 enterprise customers.
mitigations: Immediate: enabled 'emit-min-batch' fallback to ensure batch emission when slot coordination fails. Rolled back the precedence optimization on 2026-03-07 03:58 UTC for all affected runtime=1.23 clusters. Medium-term: deployed synchronization fix for slot watermark propagation (hotfix id: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/5123). Long-term: design work item to introduce deterministic slot leases and a reconciliation loop that avoids relying on GC timing.

(E) Add a runtime safety: if 'slot_inflight_count'==0 and queue_depth>threshold for >2s, auto-enable 'emit-min-batch' and route to fast-path (owner: Runtime team - lead: Marcus Liang) - due 2026-03-18 - EST: 3 - PR: github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/5201
(F) Postmortem write-up and customer communication collateral (owner: Aisha Patel) - due 2026-03-15 - EST: 2 - doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ENG/ENG-81234+postmortem
decision_log: Decisions taken during incident: (1) Roll back precedence optimization to restore prior fairness behaviour (approved by Runtime PM). (2) Prioritize deterministic lease design over repeated micro-guards (trade-off: short-term complexity for long-term correctness). (3) Accept a small CPU overhead (~2%) from per-request jitter to significantly reduce alignment probability. Notes: decisions reviewed with PM (Evan Brooks) and SRE (Diego Marquez) 2026-03-07 06:15 UTC.
follow_up_notes: We observed that the revert reduced recurrence but did not eliminate brief stalls under heavy routing churn. The deterministic lease design must be complemented by more robust reconciliation (heartbeats + bounded retries). Consider adding an integration test in CI that injects delayed watermark propagation. Also review related tickets ENG-74219 and ENG-61457 for backloged fairness improvements to reuse prior work.
